newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arctic seeks global offensive against pollution.
newsitem.headline: Arctic seeks global offensive against pollution.

text.p: A global effort must be made to fight pollution accumulating in the Arctic that has contaminated its people and wildlife with toxins, Norway's environment minister told the U.N. Earth Summit on Wednesday.
"The issues have become global issues," Norwegian Environment Minister Torbjoern Berntsen told a briefing.
"There is mounting pressure on the unique and vulnerable environment of the Arctic," he said.

"The Arctic is the final storage of many contaminants used on a global scale" such as heavy metals, persistent organic chemicals and radioactive wastes, Lars Erik Liljelund, of the Arctic Monitoring Assessment Programme (AMEP), said.
That programme was launched in 1991 to track effects of pollution that are carried by water and winds to a final resting place in the Arctic.

It has found that Arctic women, particularly in eastern Canada and western Greenland, have body levels of persistent organic chemicals, like DDT pesticides, that are near or exceed levels likely to produce problems in their children.
Such chemicals and heavy metals "biomagnify" as they climb the food chain to indigenous Arctic people who depend on fish and wildlife for food, Liljelund said.
Many Arctic people carry levels of mercury 5 to 12 times higher than the population at lower latitudes, and this contamination is increasing, he said.
Radioactivity from the Chernobyl nuclear disaster and nuclear weapons testing also exposes Arctic people to higher radiation levels than in temperate zones, Liljelund and Bersten said.

The Arctic is specially vulnerable to the effects of global warming, although Liljelund said there is still some question whether changes so far have been from natural causes or man-made heat-trapping pollution.

Liljelund said if global warming worsened, the Arctic would lose its property of being a "sink" or absorber of carbon gases causing global warming, and would instead become a contributor because of decaying vegetation.
